plate.viewWhy: Census view is side; the heels rising above and dipping below the step edge (c2, c4), the straight but unlocked knee (c7) and the upright body read from the side. The top fault, moving too quickly or bouncing (c9), shows only as speed, so the plate draws partial range (c8), the heels stopping part way.
plate.equipment: Generic box or step (census box) under the forefoot with the heels free (c2, c3), floor line (census floor). Motra teaches the raise on flat ground and allows a step for the stretch (c2, c13); the census note draws the forefoot on an edge.
plate.start: Bottom of the rep: standing tall, feet hip-width, toes forward (c1); balls of the feet on the step edge, heels flat or slightly below it for a stretch (c2, c3); knees straight but unlocked (c7); arms by the sides, or hands on a wall for balance (c1). No source gives joint angles.
plate.end: Top of the rep: on the tiptoes, heels as high as possible (c4); knees still straight but unlocked (c7); body unchanged.

mistake.what: Heels moving only part way up or down.
mistake.why: The top fault, moving too quickly or bouncing, which Peloton's coach calls the most common mistake he sees (c9), shows only as speed, so the plate draws the next fault by the same steps: partial range, next on Motra's common-mistakes list (c8), against its full range from on the toes to flat or slightly below a step (c2).
mistake.rankNote: No source measures how often each fault happens. LR-31 step 1: moving too quickly or bouncing through the motion (c9). Peloton, under 'Common Mistakes to Avoid' for the calf raise: "“The most common mistake I see is people moving too quickly or bouncing through the motion,” Matt says." The sentence before ties it to this exercise ("The calf raise may be a simple exercise, but proper form matters."), and the version taught on the page is the bodyweight standing raise, so it counts as a step-1 hit for this exercise's own fault (D-SUP-LB7-DIPREPS). It is not a list sentence read onto one item: it states the frequency itself. Motra's list item 1, "Bouncing at bottom" (c8), is the same fault. Set aside at step 1: Peloton's "A common starting point is 2-3 sets of 8-12 repetitions" (c14) is programming; Peloton's heading "Common Mistakes to Avoid" is a heading, not a frequency word. Garage Gym Reviews' "commonly neglected calf muscles" is about the muscles, "this often-overlooked muscle group" and "answering common questions" about the muscles and the article, "Most calf workouts will target the gastrocnemius and the soleus" about training, "Calf presses are most often performed using a leg press machine." another exercise, and "give your muscle fibers time to recover fully, usually about forty-eight hours" programming; Motra's "Popularity Score" is about the exercise. drawable false: moving too quickly or bouncing shows only as speed (LR-31). The plate draws the next fault by the same steps. Step 1 has no other hit. Step 2: no other named fault is tied to harm: Motra's "Avoid hyperextension of knees" (c7) and "Use support for balance" (c11) state no harm; its "Stop if Achilles pain occurs" (c10) names no fault; its "When to Avoid" items are conditions; Peloton's "reduce injury risk", "further reducing the risk of ankle sprains", "may also help reduce the risk of injury", its Achilles overuse study line and "especially when joint movement is painful" are about the exercise's benefits and its isometric variation, not a fault; Garage Gym Reviews' "more likely going to leave you sore and at risk of injury" is about training the calves every day, and its "approximately 50% immediate reduction in Achilles tendon pain" is the isometric hold, another exercise. Step 3: the first remaining fault on the common-mistakes list written for this exercise, in source order (Motra, c8; Peloton's section names only the speed fault): partial range (c8), which the side view shows as the heels stopping part way. handlingMistakes: [0] moving too fast or bouncing (step 1), [1] partial range, [2] locking the knees, in Motra's list order.

tells.text: Heels rise as high as possible

tempo.text: Down 2 and up 2 are Motra's 2-1-2 (c15, WEAK), read in its Tempo tooltip's order: lowering, bottom pause, lifting, top pause (R-LB6-2, R-LB6-7); the page shows three numbers, read as the first three. Its 1 s bottom pause is named here and not written in pause (LR-33). Pause 1 is the hold right after the lift: Peloton's "Hold the top position for a second or two" (c5, c15) gives seconds, and the plate draws the low end, 1 s; Motra's "hold briefly" and Garage Gym Reviews' "Pause" (c5) agree. Peloton's eccentric variation lowers over 3-5 seconds on one leg and its coach's "rising quickly to build power and lowering slowly" is for athletic performance; neither is this tempo.

Anchor: Motra's bodyweight calf raise page, read in full (How to Perform, Coaching Tips, Tempo with its tooltip, Range of Motion, Safety, Common Mistakes). Peloton's calf-raise article and Garage Gym Reviews' calf-exercises page were read in full; only GGR's section 1 (Basic Calf Raises (Bodyweight)) is cited. The fetcher's scan covered GGR through section 1; the writer scanned sections 2-15, the FAQs and the references for LR-31 and LR-33 words (2026-10-22): no frequency or harm word about a calf-raise fault (hits: "Calf presses are most often performed using a leg press machine", "especially helpful in strengthening the calf muscle after an injury", the isometric hold's Achilles pain line, "leave you sore and at risk of injury" and "usually about forty-eight hours" on daily training, all set aside in the rankNote or naming no fault); pause words only in other exercises' steps ("Pause, then slowly return" in sections 2, 3 and 5, "Hold briefly, then release." in the calf press, "Hold the position" in the seated barbell raise and the isometric hold).

Surface: Motra describes the raise on flat ground and lowers 'to flat or slightly below if on step' (c2); Peloton says a step or curb gives more range (c2). The census draws the forefoot on a box edge, so the card's setup puts the lifter on a step; the heels-hanging-off line comes from Peloton's eccentric variation steps (c3, WEAK).
Stance width: Motra and Peloton say hip-width; Garage Gym Reviews says shoulder-width (c1). The card follows hip-width.

The Achilles feel row and risk keep Motra's stop quote (c10, "Stop if Achilles pain occurs"; R-LB3-4, R-LB6-6). No shared red-flag box covers the ankle, so its redFlag is null. The knee row is place + the source's fault + fix (LR-6), linking the knee box.

Read and not cited: ACE's Calf Raises page (exercise-library/51) is the barbell version, another version. Healthline, Verywell Fit (402) and StrengthLog's bodyweight calf raise page (429) could not be used.
